subject: scientist
label: scientist, in the place of the game's models/scientist.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/gman.mdl, models/hassassin.mdl, models/barney.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, A, D, C where the asset was D, B, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The brief's man in a lab coat is readable, but the outline is clearly off. In FRONT, BACK and TOP the head is a squat block sitting straight on wide, bulky shoulders with no neck, and the arms hang as thick tubes. In LEFT and RIGHT the body is a wide coat mass with thin legs underneath. Proportions do not read as an older man of normal build.

M2.reason: Height measures 68.4 against the brief's 68 (0.7% off), well within 15%. The brief gives no length or width, so those are not held to a figure. Measured 23.4 long and 31.6 wide, both plausible for a standing man with arms out.

M3.reason: Parts the brief names that all three Valve models in the line-up also show are present: the head, both arms and hands, both legs, and the feet in dark shoes. The white coat, the blue shirt with a red tie at the front (front view), and the light tan trousers are there. Glasses and grey hair are named by the brief but not shown by every Valve model beside it, so their absence is not charged. The shapes of the head and hands are crude (see M1), but no named part is missing.

M4.reason: White coat, blue shirt, red tie and tan trousers with dark boots match the brief's colours. The head's top is pink-orange skin tone where the brief says balding with grey hair, so the hair region has the wrong colour and material. Hands and face read as skin.

M5.reason: Pocket lines and a few shirt marks show on the coat front (FRONT, FRONT-RIGHT). The glasses, which are surface detail the brief names, are not readable, and the face has no visible features. Black slivers at the right hip (RIGHT, BACK-RIGHT) and the left hip (FRONT-RIGHT) look like stray dark marks rather than designed detail.

M6.reason: Scored 2 as the rubric caps M6 for this measure. Line-up test: four readings, the asset at D, B, C, C in turn, and the judges picked D, A, D, C. Two picks landed on the asset, a little above chance, below the catch line of three of four, so the line-up does not catch it. Beside the Valve models, the head and hands look cruder than Valve's, which is noted here, but the test result stands.

M7.reason: Front is correct: the tie and coat buttons face forward in FRONT, and the figure stands upright on its feet with the boots on the floor line in LEFT and RIGHT. Feet sit on the origin without floating or sinking.

M8.reason: Triangles are 1196, under the 1640 that Valve's most-detailed model of the kind spends, so the triangle measure passes; the SMAK check reports no errors. Black slivers at the right hip (RIGHT, BACK-RIGHT) and left hip (FRONT-RIGHT) may be open or inside-out faces. A player can see them from outside, so 'nothing open' is not confirmed.

C1.reason: Across the eight run frames and eight shotgun frames, legs stay under the coat, arms stay on the shoulders, and the head stays on the body. Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The stride reads as a run and the attack reads as a raised, hugged-in arm pose.
